title: Canonical cochain shifts of semilinear system operations
statement: Let $u$ be a universe, $C:\mathbb N\to\operatorname{CommRing}$ a sequence of commutative rings in universe $u+1$, and $\tau_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$ arbitrary ring homomorphisms. For schemes in universe $u$, use the strict semilinear systems $\mathscr S_X$, their ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_X$, the ordinary inverse image $v^*_\bullet$, direct image $v_{*,\bullet}$, open extension $j_{!,\bullet}$ and their derived operations $P_v$, $R_v$, $J_j$ of [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations]. For any cochain complex $M$ and integer $h$, use $M[h]^p=M^{p+h}$ and $d_{M[h]}^p=(-1)^h d_M^{p+h}$. Define the integer-shift structure on $P_v$ to be the one induced by the exact termwise functor $v^*_\bullet$ on complexes and its localization. For any open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, define the integer-shift structure on $J_j$ to be the one induced by the exact termwise functor $j_{!,\bullet}$ and its localization. Define the integer-shift structure on $R_v$ to be its standard right-derived, K-injective shift structure: shift a K-injective representative, apply $v_{*,\bullet}$ termwise and use the standard localization comparisons. Each structure consists of the canonical natural isomorphisms $F(M[h])\cong F(M)[h]$ with their zero and addition coherence. These definitions impose no flatness, boundedness, constructibility or nonemptiness assumptions.
